source_text: Quid nunc, gentiles? Creditis Christianos sentire carceris poenas et saeculares horrere tenebras, quos manet gaudium lucis aeternae? Spiritus cum fida spe uenientis gratiae caelos mente complexus, suis iam non interest poenis. Secretam licet suppliciis quaeratis et abditam sedem, graues antri caligantis horrores domumque tenebrarum, fidentibus in deum nullus squalidus locus, nullum tempus triste sentitur. Fouet illos deo patri dicatos fratres diebus Christus et noctibus. Etenim Mariano post illam uexationem corporis altius in soporis tranquilla resoluto, quid diuina dignatio ad fiduciam spei salutaris ostenderit, expergefactus nobis sic ipse narrauit: Ostensum est, inquit, mihi, fratres, tribunalis excelsi et candidi nimium sublime fastigium, in quo ad uicem praesidis iudex satis decora facie praesidebat. Illic erat catasta, non humili pulpitu nec uno tantum ascensibilis gradu, sed multis ordinata gradibus et longe sublimis ascensu. Et admouebantur confessorum singulae classes, quas ille iudex ad gladium duci iubebat. Uentum est et ad me. Tunc exauditur mihi uox clara et inmensa dicentis: Marianum applica. Et ascendebam in illam catastam, et ecce ex inprouiso mihi sedens ad dexteram eius iudicis Cyprianus apparuit et porrexit manum et leuauit me in altiorem catastae locum, et arrisit et ait: Ueni, sede mecum. Et factum est ut audirentur aliae classes, me quoque assidente. Et surrexit ille iudex, et nos eum deducebamus ad praetorium suum. Iter autem nobis erat per locum pratis amoenum et uirentium nemorum laeta fronde uestitum, opacum cupressis consurgentibus in excelsum et pinis pulsantibus caelum, ut putares eum locum per omnem circuitus ambitum lucis uirentibus coronatum. Sinus autem in medio perlucidi fontis uberantibus uenis et puris liquoribus redundabat. Et ecce subito ab oculis nostris ille iudex recessit. Tunc ibi Cyprianus fialam, quae super marginem fontis iacebat, arripuit, et cum illam de fonte sitienti similis inplesset, hausit, et inplens iterum mihi porrexit, et libenter bibi. Et cum Deo gratias dicerem, excitatus, inquit, mea uoce, surrexi.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: What then, Gentiles? Do you believe Christians feel prison's punishments and shudder at worldly darkness, whom joy of eternal light awaits? The spirit, having embraced the heavens in mind with faithful hope of coming grace, is now not concerned with its own punishments. Although you seek a hidden place for tortures and a concealed seat, the oppressive horrors of a darkening cave and a house of darkness, for those trusting in God no squalid place, no sad time is felt. Christ cherishes by days and by nights those brothers dedicated to God the Father. For with Marianus, after that harassment of the body, more deeply released into the calm of sleep, what divine condescension showed for assurance of saving hope, awakened he himself told us thus: There was shown to me, he says, brothers, the very lofty height of a tribunal high and shining white, on which in place of the governor a judge of sufficiently comely face presided. There was a scaffold, accessible not by a low platform nor by only one step, but arranged with many steps and far lofty in ascent. And the several ranks of confessors were brought forward, whom that judge ordered to be led to the sword. It came also to me. Then a clear and vast voice of one saying is heard by me: Bring Marianus forward. And I was ascending onto that scaffold, and behold unexpectedly Cyprian, sitting at the right hand of that judge, appeared to me and extended his hand and lifted me to a higher place of the scaffold, and smiled and said: Come, sit with me. And it happened that other ranks were heard, with me also sitting beside. And that judge rose, and we escorted him to his residence. But our path was through a place pleasant with meadows and clothed with joyous foliage of green groves, shaded by cypresses rising on high and pines striking heaven, so that you would think that place crowned through the whole compass of its circuit with the green things of light. But in the middle a hollow overflowed with the gushing veins and pure waters of a clear spring. And behold suddenly that judge withdrew from our eyes. Then there Cyprian seized a bowl which lay on the edge of the spring, and when like a thirsty man he had filled it from the spring, he drank, and filling again he extended it to me, and I drank willingly. And when I was giving thanks to God, roused, he says, by my own voice, I rose.
pass_b_english: What now, Gentiles? Do you suppose that Christians feel the punishments of prison and shudder at earthly darkness, when the joy of eternal light awaits them? The spirit, embracing heaven in thought with faithful hope of the grace to come, no longer attends to its own sufferings. Though you seek out for their torments a secret and hidden lodging, the crushing horrors of a gloomy cavern and a house of darkness, for those who trust in God no place is felt as squalid and no time as sorrowful. Christ comforts, by day and by night, those brothers who are dedicated to God the Father.

For when Marianus, after that affliction of his body, had sunk more deeply into the stillness of sleep, he himself, once awakened, told us what the divine condescension had shown him for the assurance of saving hope: There was shown to me, brothers, he said, the exceeding lofty height of a tribunal, white and radiant, on which, in the governor's place, a judge of most comely countenance presided. There stood a scaffold, reached not by a low platform nor by a single step alone, but ordered with many steps and rising far aloft in its ascent. And the separate companies of confessors were led up, whom that judge ordered to be led away to the sword. My turn came too. Then a clear and immense voice was heard by me, saying: Bring Marianus forward. And I was climbing that scaffold, and behold, suddenly Cyprian appeared to me, seated at the right hand of that judge, and he stretched out his hand and raised me to a higher place on the scaffold, and smiled and said: Come, sit with me. And other companies were called on, while I sat beside him too. And that judge rose, and we conducted him to his palace. Our way lay through a place lovely with meadows and clad in the glad foliage of green groves, shaded by cypresses rising on high and pines reaching to heaven, so that you would have thought the whole circle of that place crowned round about with living green. In its midst a hollow basin overflowed with the gushing veins and pure streams of a crystal spring. And behold, suddenly that judge vanished from our eyes. Then Cyprian seized there a bowl lying on the margin of the spring, and when he had filled it from the spring like one athirst, he drank deeply, and filling it again he held it out to me, and I drank gladly. And while I was giving thanks to God, roused, he said, by my own voice, I awoke.
